title: handoff-orbit-standup-summary-2027-12-28
notes:
Purpose: weekly sync for Solutions Engineering + Pro Services to align prioritization, unblock customer integrations, and confirm handoffs for next sprint.

Attendees: Priya Nair (SE lead), Liam O'Neill (ProServices PM), Hana Suzuki (Field Eng), Carlos Rivera (SRE), Maya Patel (Customer Success), plus engineers on call from infra and runtime.

High-level status: overall momentum steady but capacity risk for late-January launches. Three active customers discussed in depth (AtlasPay, Meridian Retail, Nebula Health).

AtlasPay (payments platform) — status: staging to prod handoff in progress
- Current sprint: finishing PCI compliance checklist, integration test matrix, and load-safety harness. Nightly end-to-end smoke runs pass 94% of checks; remaining failures are rate-limit edge cases.
- SLOs agreed: 95th-percentile latency < 220ms for token generation at peak traffic for dedicated pool; availability 99.9% during business hours.
- Blockers: quota increase request for dedicated capacity (requested 4x current pilot allocation), pending procurement approval. Also, test card throttling surfaced a tokenization race condition in client adapter.
- Decisions: freeze model variant to 7b-quant-v2 for initial rollout to simplify kernel paths. ProServices to own the adapter patch; SE to provide test vectors.

Meridian Retail (POC -> canary) — status: canary preparing
- Current sprint: canary config drafted to run 5% traffic on Dedicated cluster in us-west-2 with KV-cache enabled and dynamic batching disabled for determinism.
- Observability: instrumentation hooks added for per-route token cost reporting; first dashboard draft deployed to Console preview.
- Blockers: anomaly in prompt truncation when combined with client-side prompt templates — causes mismatch between expected token accounting and runtime outputs.
- Decision: postpone opening canary to real user traffic until prompt-truncation fix lands. Short-term workaround: server-side rigid prompt-truncation flag toggled by route.

Nebula Health (private/VPC) — status: compliance and network
- Current sprint: private control plane deployment automated via terraform modules; internal review of KMS integration ongoing.
- Compliance: SOC2 readiness checklist complete; customer requested additional audit trail for model rollouts.
- Blockers: customer requires HSM-backed signing for model artifacts; product team flagged dependency on third-party HSM provider certifications.
- Action: Security & Compliance to scope an interim TAP using our KMS + auditable attestations while we validate HSM vendor compatibility.

Operational notes and cross-customer themes:
- Capacity planning: January surge forecast shows 60% chance of oversubscription in us-west-2 for dedicated pools if Meridian goes to canary while AtlasPay scales. Recommend burst-policy limit increases and prioritization gating for enterprise rollouts.
- Observability gaps: token-level cost attribution exists but per-route cold-start percentiles are noisy. SRE to add histogram smoothing and retention to 90 days for key routes.
- Rollouts & fallbacks: agreed to standardize canary to 1/5/20% progression with automatic fallback to hosted-variant if latency exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive 5-min windows.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Freeze AtlasPay model variant to 7b-quant-v2 for first release (owner: Priya; due: 2028-01-03).
- Delay Meridian canary until prompt-truncation fix merged and two consecutive internal smoke runs pass (owner: Hana; due: 2028-01-05).
- Implement KMS-based attestation for Nebula audit requirement as interim (owner: Carlos; due: 2028-01-10).

Action items:
- Priya Nair - 2028-01-03 - produce AtlasPay release checklist and test-vector pack and attach to PROSERV-874.
- Liam O'Neill - 2028-01-04 - follow up with procurement on dedicated capacity increase for AtlasPay and escalate to GTM if no response by EOD 2028-01-05.
- Hana Suzuki - 2028-01-05 - merge prompt-truncation hotfix and run two clean smoke runs; report results in #se-proservices.
- Carlos Rivera - 2028-01-10 - prototype KMS-attestation artifacts and share terraform snippets for Nebula.
- Maya Patel - 2028-01-06 - schedule executive-facing readiness briefing with AtlasPay stakeholders after checklist completion.
- SRE on-call (TBD) - 2028-01-02 - add histogram smoothing and 90-day retention to per-route cold-start metrics; create dashboard link.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: capacity oversubscription in us-west-2 could delay both AtlasPay and Meridian launches. Mitigation: shift Meridian canary to us-east-1 if AtlasPay capacity request is approved; pre-warm extra nodes.
- Risk: HSM vendor certification timelines could push Nebula private launch beyond Q1. Mitigation: provide interim KMS attestations and clear customer-facing timeline.
- Risk: prompt-truncation bug may cause user-visible output truncation in Meridian POC. Mitigation: mandatory server-side truncation flag until client libs patched.

Next meeting: Weekly SE + ProServices sync — 2028-01-04 09:30 PT. Pre-reads: AtlasPay checklist draft, Meridian smoke-run logs, Nebula KMS prototype link.

Notes to self: include short checklist template for canary gating in the repo under serving-config/canary-templates; ensure PR for instrumentation uses small default retention to avoid billing surprises.

Key outcomes: model freeze for AtlasPay, Meridian canary postponed pending prompt fix, and KMS attestation path chosen as interim for Nebula's audit needs. Capacity in us-west-2 is the single highest operational risk for January launches.
